swap.evidence: Products tried: a neighbourhood seed library; a council equipment-loan scheme. Survives unchanged: header with small line icon and name in bold body sans, sage ground, single green accent, bordered card grid with one generic glyph per card, government-pattern error summary, month grid. Bound to this product: only copy (tool names with specs, deposits, Mill Lane, Wed/Sat session times). With the name hidden, the wrench icon and tool names tell you what it is; the visual frame does not.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a volunteer/civic booking flow: off-white ground, one civic green or blue accent, bordered cards, GOV.UK-like forms and error summary. Predicted opposite: a warm, hand-made 'community' look with craft textures and a script face. The render matches the default on ground, accent, card list and error pattern.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservation for a toy library run by parents from a church hall'. Predicted choices: pale ground, one accent, card grid with an icon per item, month grid of open days, filled primary button. Overlap is near total; the only brief-driven choices are copy and the deposit/session details.

Copy is the only product-bound layer: tool specs, deposits, Mill Lane, session hours, the volunteer desk phone.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Detectors returned zero hits. The green accent (#1f5a3a, hue about 147 degrees) sits just outside the SLP-28 range and is in any case explained by the membership-card green in DESIGN.md. Nothing in the detector output changes the verdicts.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench icon in its thumbnail slot
findings.description: On the find page all ten cards lead with an identical pale square containing the same wrench glyph. The slot is sized like a product photo but carries no information, so it reads as a placeholder left on show.
findings.impact: Members looking for 'the drill with two batteries' get no visual help telling tools apart, and the most prominent repeated element on the entry page makes the site look unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail slot is for: photographs of the library's own stock, or a per-category drawing system that actually differs, or remove the slot so the name and availability lead.

findings.title: Tool names truncate at 375 px so similar tools become indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 px card titles are cut with an ellipsis: both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', the ladder 'Extension ladder 3 m ...'. The distinguishing detail (one vs two batteries, length) is the part removed.
findings.impact: On phones, the main device, members may open the wrong drill; it undercuts the DESIGN.md rule 'name tools the way a volunteer would' and the 'careful' attribute.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap on narrow widths; decide whether the thumbnail earns its width there.

findings.title: Search moves below the whole tool list on phones
findings.description: At 375 px the 'Search tools' field and filter toggle are placed after all ten cards, while at 768 px and up they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Members with a tool in mind, mostly on phones, may not find search without scrolling past the entire stock; the page's job is 'find a tool'.
findings.recommendation: Keep the source and visual order the same at every width with search before results.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unstyled native date and select controls with a non-en-GB date pattern
findings.description: The open filter panel shows a native date input reading 'yyyy/mm/dd' and a native select whose height, radius and label baseline differ from the 44 px styled inputs; the Category label sits lower than 'Available from'.
findings.impact: The panel looks unfinished beside the styled search, and the date pattern contradicts the declared format 'Saturday 17 October', which may confuse older members.
findings.recommendation: Bring the filter controls onto the input component tokens and align the two fields on one baseline; decide how dates are entered in the declared format.

findings.title: Basket sessions run latest-first in a lopsided 1 + 5 layout
findings.description: Pick-up sessions are listed from Wednesday 28 October down to Saturday 10 October. At 1280 the first sits alone at full width and the other five are squeezed into narrow tiles with three-line wraps; sessions before the chosen pick-up day (Saturday 17 October) are still offered.
findings.impact: The member's natural choice (their pick-up day) is buried mid-list and the layout gives the furthest date the most weight; it may lead to choosing a wrong session.
findings.recommendation: Order sessions chronologically from the chosen day and give every option the same layout treatment.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x~224 while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x~180, so one list has two ragged value edges, at 1280 and 375.
findings.impact: Reads as two lists stitched together and slows scanning of the specs members compare between similar tools.
findings.recommendation: Treat the details as one description list with one label column.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar has no month heading
findings.description: The month grid on the tool page starts with weekday letters and day numbers 9 to 29, with no 'October 2026' heading or month navigation visible in any captured width.
findings.impact: Members must infer the month from the 'Available from' line; the one product-specific device loses clarity.

evidence.detail: no month label above the Su-Sa row

findings.recommendation: Label the grid with its month.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the fill from 'Available' chips but keeps it on later dates
findings.description: In dark mode 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' renders as green text with no chip fill, while 'Available from Sat 17 Oct' and later keep a grey filled chip, so the less available items look more emphasised.
findings.impact: Emphasis inverts between themes; dark mode is common among members, who may read the filled chips as the bookable ones.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge-available token so the chip keeps a visible fill distinct from the later-date chip.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar sits off the content grid at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280 the action bar spans the viewport in white over the sage ground and places 'Reserve this tool' at x~1077-1264, outside the 1184 px content edge every other element aligns to; in captures it also covers part of the calendar.
findings.impact: The page's primary action looks detached from the form it completes on desktop; the decision to place it for thumbs makes less sense at 1280.
findings.recommendation: Align the bar's contents to the page content width at wide viewports.

findings.title: Short pages leave an empty band below the footer at desktop widths
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280 the white footer ends mid-viewport and a flat sage band fills the rest of the screen.
findings.impact: Makes the confirmation and basket pages look unfinished at the moment members commit.
findings.recommendation: Keep the footer at the bottom of the viewport on short pages.

findings.title: Done page has no confirmation moment and still shows 'Basket (1)'
findings.description: 'Reservation confirmed' is set like every other page heading with no success treatment, and the header still reads 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is made.
findings.impact: Members may be unsure whether the tool is reserved or still waiting in the basket.
findings.recommendation: Use the declared success notice for the confirmation and clear the basket count.

findings.title: 'Added to your basket' toast covers the calendar weekday header
findings.description: In the added state at 1280 the toast sits over the We/Th column headings of the pick-up calendar.
findings.impact: Hides part of the control the member just used; minor.
findings.recommendation: Place the toast where it does not cover the form.

strengths: Copy in the volunteer's voice, concrete and kind: specs a borrower needs, deposits everywhere, 'Nothing is paid online'.
A composed dark theme (lighter cards on dark ground, mint primary, salmon errors) rather than an inversion.
Error summary plus inline messages on basket and confirm, with examples ('like FT-01234').
One filled button per page, honoured on every surface.
keep: Keep the conventional, one-action-per-page structure and the volunteer voice; add identity on top of them rather than replacing them.
not_assessable: No baseline screenshots: pairwise not applicable.
Motion (120 ms fades), focus rendering and sticky-bar scroll behaviour cannot be judged from stills.
